entry.title: Nobel Prize for Halzen
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Royal Swedish Academy of Science announced the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for Francis Halzen, IceCube principal investigator, for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. Wisconsin Public Radio interviewed him on the prize and the importance of neutrino research. The whole South Pole station gathered at the IceCube Lab for a group photo when the award became known.

entry.title: DUNE sensor production
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. UK scientists and engineers have completed half of the 137 Anode Plane Assemblies for DUNE. These sensors will detect the small electrical signals produced when neutrinos interact with liquid argon in DUNE's underground detectors.

A separate report describes marine operations for ARCA and ORCA, including installation of Cable Termination Frame 3 at the ARCA deep-sea site.

entry.title: JUNO-TAO first data
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The JUNO Collaboration reports commissioning performance and first results from the Taishan Antineutrino Observatory, a satellite of JUNO. It uses a 2.8-ton liquid-scintillator detector with 4,024 silicon photomultiplier tiles, 43.2 m from a reactor core, to measure the reactor antineutrino spectrum. Installation was completed in 2025 and physics data taking began on 10 February 2026. Stable cryogenic operation has been achieved.

entry.title: Baikal-GVD point sources
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Baikal-GVD is under construction in Lake Baikal and is now 70% complete. A search for point-like sources in its 2019-2024 track-like dataset found no significant source, so the authors compute upper limits for selected candidate objects and compare them with published IceCube, ANTARES and KM3NeT results.

entry.title: P-ONE photomultipliers
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. P-ONE is a planned cubic-kilometre-scale neutrino telescope for the Pacific Ocean, using Ocean Networks Canada infrastructure. A new paper characterises all the photomultiplier tubes for the first detector line before deployment, to ensure they meet the detector acceptance criteria. That line will use 320 3-inch R14374-10 tubes.

entry.title: IceCube infrared flares
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. IceCube has published a search for high-energy neutrinos from infrared flares. It is motivated by the neutrino emission seen from the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068, and by external candidate associations such as AT2019dsg and AT2019fdr. The record excerpt does not give the outcome of the search.

entry.title: T2K ND280 upgrade
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The ND280 upgrade was completed in 2024. Its SuperFGD is a segmented scintillator detector of about 2 million optically isolated 1 cm³ cubes read out by three orthogonal wavelength-shifting fibres. A new event selection for muon-neutrino charged-current interactions with single positively charged pion production targets the new modules, as a step towards reducing the dominant systematic uncertainties of the oscillation analysis.

entry.title: NνDEx simulation framework
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. NνDEx is designed to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of 82Se and is planned for the China Jinping Underground Laboratory. It will use a high-pressure 82SeF6 gas TPC with Topmetal pixelated readout. A new paper presents a full simulation and reconstruction framework built on the REST toolkit.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, which are expected to contain Δ isobars if observed massive stars include heavier baryons. It matters for neutron-star thermal evolution, where nucleonic and hyperonic Urca processes are the dominant cooling mechanisms.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper extends the Standard Model with a gauged U(1) Lμ−Lτ symmetry and an ultralight vector boson, which modifies solar-neutrino MSW oscillations through kinetic mixing with the photon. It uses Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande solar data and discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD.

entry.title: The authors calculate two-neutrino double-beta decay rates without decoupling nuclear structure from the lepto
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors calculate two-neutrino double-beta decay rates without decoupling nuclear structure from the lepton kinematics, and compare with closure, non-closure and Taylor-expansion approximations for 82Se and 136Xe. This bears on the two-neutrino spectrum and rate, which underlie neutrinoless double-beta decay searches in these isotopes.

entry.title: The paper assesses whether nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals could register neutrinos from past Galact
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper assesses whether nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals could register neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae. It varies neutron-star masses and includes failed supernovae that form black holes, and examines the role of the nuclear equation of state. Sensitivity is larger for models with larger neutrino emission.

entry.title: The paper examines thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, in which neutrino masses arise
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper examines thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, in which neutrino masses arise from a dimension-7 operator at tree level and a dimension-5 operator at one loop. The model accommodates sub-eV neutrino masses with new physics at the TeV scale. The authors state that leptogenesis here differs from the canonical seesaw case.

entry.title: The paper considers magnetic and oscillation effects on neutrinos from a protoneutron star in a supernova
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper considers magnetic and oscillation effects on neutrinos from a protoneutron star in a supernova. It finds that oscillations in the outer stellar layers harden the electron antineutrino spectrum, most strongly for the inverted mass ordering. This is relevant to the dependence of ground-based supernova-neutrino detection on the mass ordering.
